evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/realtors.rs:135-143 (create_profile) maps the repo error via `e.to_string().contains("already exists")` -> HTTP 400, else generic 500; and :173-183 (update_profile) maps `error_str.contains("not found")` -> HTTP 404, else 500. Classifying DB/repo failures by substring-matching the error's Display text is fragile: the matched text originates in the sqlx/Postgres driver or repository layer and is not a stable contract. A driver/dependency upgrade, a localized or reworded message, or a different error variant that happens to (or no longer) contains the magic substring silently reclassifies outcomes -- e.g. a genuine transient DB failure that stops containing "not found" would surface as a 500 instead of 404, or (worse direction) a real failure whose text incidentally contains the substring would be masked as a benign 400/404 to the client.

Same stringly-typed anti-pattern also appears in routes/agencies.rs:439 (`error_str.contains("permission") || error_str.contains("unauthorized")` -> FORBIDDEN). Net-new for the realtors/agencies handlers: the only prior error-string-status finding (code-review-reality-server-saved-search-error-string-status) is on a different saved-search handler.
Fix: map repository results via typed error variants (an enum or sqlx::Error discriminants / a NotFound/Conflict domain error) rather than substring scans of Display output.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/email.rs:179-184 -- SmtpPasswordResetMailer::new, when `settings.use_tls` is false, builds the transport via `AsyncSmtpTransport::<Tokio1Executor>::builder_dangerous(&settings.host)` and then attaches `.credentials(creds)` (:184). `use_tls` is derived at :152-154 from `SMTP_TLS` (`v != "false" && v != "0"`, default true). If an operator sets SMTP_TLS=false (or mistypes it to any value parsing as false), the password-reset mailer performs SMTP AUTH over a plaintext connection -- username+password sent in cleartext -- with NO warning emitted (build_password_reset_mailer at :280-303 only logs the happy-path 'SMTP transport configured' info; there is no log distinguishing the TLS vs builder_dangerous branch).

Impact: LOW (requires explicit operator opt-in) but a real credential-exposure footgun: the cleartext-AUTH path is silent, so a misconfiguration leaks SMTP credentials on the wire with no operational signal. Unlike LogPasswordResetMailer (which deliberately warns in release and gates the token behind debug_assertions), the dangerous SMTP branch has no equivalent guard rail.

Fix: emit a `tracing::warn!` when the dangerous/non-TLS transport is selected (or refuse to attach credentials to a non-TLS transport in release builds), so plaintext SMTP AUTH can never be used silently.
